title: paged-kv-cache: locality-aware pinning + allocator reuse to reduce fragmentation and tail latency
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: The paged KV cache block manager suffers from fragmentation and suboptimal placement for hot token sequences which increases tail latency and memory churn under realistic chat workloads. This PR implements a locality-aware pinning policy and refactors the block allocator to favor reuse of recently freed contiguous regions, reducing fragmentation and improving cache hit stability.

Summary of changes (high level):
- Add a locality-aware pinning heuristic: pin blocks that are frequently accessed together and prefer co-locating allocations for the same request/session to improve prefetch/KV locality.
- Refactor BlockAllocator to maintain per-size free lists with an MRU preference and a small lookahead to merge adjacent free blocks for contiguous allocation -> reduces scatter across pages.
- Introduce pin tokens and a lightweight epoch-based pin bitmap to avoid expensive refcounting races in the hot path. Pins are held for the lifetime of a request and released at end-of-request; the epoch fence ensures safe reuse without global locking.
- Add adaptive reuse thresholds: blocks younger than N ms are preferred for reuse; cold blocks are reclaimed based on TTL and aggregate fragmentation heuristics. Threshold N is tunable via config (defaults chosen from perf runs).
- Add unit and integration tests for allocator reuse, pin/unpin correctness, and concurrent allocation under synthetic workload.
- Performance harness updates and new microbenchmarks that exercise multi-stream chat workloads to measure tail latency and throughput.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc updated (links in the description to internal design)
- [x] Unit tests added for allocation/pinning semantics
- [x] Integration tests for concurrent access patterns
- [x] Microbenchmarks showing improvements
- [x] Feature flagged behind "paged_kv_locality_pinning" runtime flag for staged rollout

Important implementation notes:
- The pin bitmap uses an epoch to avoid atomic refcount increments in the critical path; we only take an expensive path when an allocation wants to reuse a pinned block. This change reduced allocation latency under contention in our microbenchmarks.
- The allocator merge/lookup keeps per-page small headers; memory overhead measured <0.5% of cache size.
- The locality heuristic tracks short-lived co-access sets via a tiny LRU per-session and emits soft hints to the allocator; hints are advisory and do not block allocations.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Default: feature disabled. We will enable behind runtime flag for canary fleet.
- No on-disk format changes; eviction/TTL semantics preserved.

How this was validated:
- Microbenchmarks: end-to-end throughput + 99th latency across 3 representative chat workloads: baseline -> 1.0x, this change -> 1.12x throughput; 99th latency reduced ~18-28% depending on workload density.
- CI: unit/integration/perf checks included.
- Dogfood: ran on a 40-GPU internal canary with spillover enabled for 48 hours; memory fragmentation metrics showed 35% fewer non-contiguous allocations and reduced OOM incidents on synthetic heavy-reuse traces.

Notes for reviewers: focus on correctness of epoch-based pinning, potential ABA/race windows, and perf model parameters. The allocator changes are isolated behind the BlockAllocator interface; the public paged-kv API remains unchanged.

Small illustrative snippet (example allocator preference): // prefer contiguous free block ranges; lookahead merges up to 4 adjacent free chunks
if (try_allocate_contiguous(request_size)) return ptr; // fallback: MRU-free-list reuse
return allocate_from_mru_list(size_class);

release_notes: Improves paged KV cache block allocation locality and reduces fragmentation; introduces experimental locality-aware pinning behind runtime flag. Expect reduced 99th token latency and fewer OOMs for heavy chat workloads. Feature off by default; enable via runtime flag for canary rollout.
